prohibitedWording: Certificate III contains no renovation training.
reasonProhibited: This overstates the evidence position and collapses a curriculum question into an absolute claim.
approvedWording: Certificate III in Carpentry includes competencies relevant to repair, alteration and existing-building work. Whether it provides a complete and consistently assessed pathway for advanced existing-home renovation capability remains a separate evidence question.
qualifiedAlternative: Do not represent curriculum scope as a binary yes-or-no proposition without current source review.
notes: Not automatically approved for all contexts until linked source claims are governed.

prohibitedWording: Handoff automatically transfers liability to a builder.
reasonProhibited: This states a legal conclusion that is not supported by the current governed evidence set.
approvedWording: Scope-escalation triggers require affected work to stop, conditions to be documented and the appropriate contractual, permit, engineering, insurance and practitioner responsibilities to be resolved before work resumes.
qualifiedAlternative: Keep wording procedural and avoid asserting automatic liability outcomes.
notes: Awaiting stronger controlled evidence on contractual and insurance effects.

prohibitedWording: RRC is a backdoor builder licence.
reasonProhibited: This mischaracterises the stated policy intent and blurs builder, engineering, permit and trade boundaries.
approvedWording: The proposed pathway is intended to recognise bounded advanced carpentry competence while preserving builder, engineering, permit and licensed-trade boundaries.
qualifiedAlternative: Describe the pathway as bounded and boundary-preserving unless current evidence supports another formulation.
notes: Draft until broader implementation claims are governed.

prohibitedWording: Any carpenter with enough years of experience should qualify.
reasonProhibited: This bypasses competence assessment, legal-boundary judgment and evidence requirements.
approvedWording: Time served may support an application but cannot replace independent assessment of competence, evidence, legal boundaries and escalation judgment.
qualifiedAlternative: Years of experience may be one input, not a substitute for controlled assessment.
notes: Remain under review until assessment model claims are populated.

prohibitedWording: The final statutory model has already been decided.
reasonProhibited: This incorrectly represents the policy process as settled when multiple options remain under evaluation.
approvedWording: Standalone registration, DB-L reform, endorsement and advanced credential models remain under evaluation.
qualifiedAlternative: Present model options as still being evaluated unless a later controlled decision record says otherwise.
notes: Publication use still requires context-by-context review.

reasonProhibited: This incorrectly converts general reform context into government endorsement of one project proposal.
approvedWording: Current Victorian building reform provides a relevant policy context for evaluating advanced residential renovation carpentry within a framework of defined scope, competence, experience and accountability.
qualifiedAlternative: Keep the link to reform architecture, not endorsement.
notes: Added in the strategic pivot sprint to prevent overstatement of government support.

prohibitedWording: Government is creating a new advanced carpenter registration.
reasonProhibited: Current published reform material does not identify advanced carpenters as a proposed registration category.
approvedWording: Government is expanding practitioner registration, but advanced carpenters are not currently identified in the published reform material as a proposed category.
qualifiedAlternative: State the published limitation directly whenever practitioner-registration expansion is mentioned.
notes: Controls interpretation of expanded registration references.

reasonProhibited: The strategic pivot places capability architecture above the final statutory vehicle.
approvedWording: The initiative proposes an Advanced Residential Carpentry capability framework. RRC is one implementation option alongside potential reform of existing pathways or another proportionate model.
qualifiedAlternative: Present RRC as a serious proposed model, not the predetermined outcome.
notes: Supports capability-first positioning across policy and public materials.
